# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I cannot choose a wire. I need the Mute to report the manual’s rule and the Deaf to describe every visible marking, especially which wire positions or colours are relevant. I will use speech for the Mute and a simple open-handed request for the Deaf; the Mute can establish any needed meaning for that gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual and report its complete cutting rule to me. Also ask the Deaf to describe the display, light, and all wire markings and positions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👐"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible state: display 0. Light blue. Wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The Deaf reports display 0, a blue light, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I still do not know the manual’s rule, so cutting now would be unsafe. I am asking the Mute for the exact rule, while acknowledging the Deaf’s report with a gesture whose meaning is not yet needed.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the Deaf's report: display 0, light blue, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. What exact wire-cutting rule does the manual give for this state?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display remains 0. Light changed to orange. Wires remain 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured ?. Blind gestured ?.

The bomb’s light has changed from blue to orange while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. I still have no usable manual instruction; the reported gestures are not readable to me. I will ask the Mute to state the rule plainly, including how the orange light and display 0 affect the choice.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state the manual rule in words now. Given display 0, light now orange, and wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue, which position must I cut?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light is now yellow; wires remain red, yellow, blue. Mute gestured thumbs-up.

The Mute’s thumbs-up is not enough to identify the wire, and I cannot see gestures directly. The Deaf can see them and has already relayed tactile/visual updates to me, so I need the Mute to encode the manual’s actual instruction through gestures and have the Deaf describe those gestures in words. I will not cut until the rule identifies a position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the exact manual rule and required wire position, one gesture at a time. Deaf, please describe each gesture to me in words.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light red; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured ? ?. No gesture meanings have been established.

The Mute knows the manual but can communicate only by gesture. We can make the gestures unambiguous by defining a wire code in speech that the Mute can hear, then the Deaf can visually identify and verbally relay the chosen gesture. I will define thumbs-up as wire 1, thumbs-down as wire 2, and OK as wire 3, and ask the Mute to use exactly one of them for the correct cut in the current state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the correct wire in the current state: thumbs-up means position 1, thumbs-down means position 2, OK means position 3. Gesture exactly one of those three signs for the wire the manual requires.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light green; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute's latest signs were thumbs-up then victory sign, but they were sent before a code was established and must not be treated as an instruction. I have asked Mute to resend using a fixed wire-and-action code.
Mute gestures to Blind: [?]

I still cannot identify the required wire from the current information. The Mute’s gesture is invisible to me, but the Deaf can see it. I will restate the fixed code and ask the Mute to send exactly one code gesture; the Deaf should then report which gesture was made, allowing me to cut the corresponding wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the current state, gesture exactly one sign: thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, OK means wire 3. Do not add any other sign. Deaf, report which sign the Mute makes.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Current state: display 0; light blue; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Under our agreed code, Mute signaled ? ?: wire 2, do not cut. No wire should be cut based on this signal.

The latest relay indicates that the manual’s signal corresponds to wire 2 but explicitly says not to cut it. Since the bomb requires a cut only when the manual calls for one, I will not act on this state. I will ask the Mute to provide a separate, unambiguous action and position code for the next state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not cut now. For the next state, gesture exactly two signs: first thumbs-up means CUT and thumbs-down means DO NOT CUT; second thumbs-up means wire 1, thumbs-down means wire 2, and OK means wire 3. Deaf, report both signs in order.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light orange; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent only ?. This means do not cut, but identifies no wire. Do not cut any wire.

The current relay says “do not cut,” and no wire is identified. I will not touch the bomb. To avoid another ambiguous signal, I am asking the Mute to send only a single, named action sign next round; if it means cut, the Mute can then send the wire number separately using the agreed wire signs.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I will not cut in the current state. Next, send exactly one action sign: thumbs-up for CUT or thumbs-down for DO NOT CUT. If CUT, send the wire sign in a separate message: thumbs-up wire 1, thumbs-down wire 2, OK wire 3. Deaf, report each sign by name and in order.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent ? ?. No wire number was given; do not cut.

No cut instruction or wire number has been reliably conveyed. The state is now display 0, yellow light, and wires red/yellow/blue, but I must not infer a rule from the changing light. I will keep the bomb untouched and ask the Deaf to report the Mute’s gestures literally, rather than interpreting an incomplete pair.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send an incomplete code. If the manual says do not cut, send only thumbs-down. If it says cut, send thumbs-up followed by exactly one wire sign: thumbs-up for wire 1, thumbs-down for wire 2, OK for wire 3.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light red; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent ?, with no wire number. I cannot interpret your ? without a defined code. Do not cut yet; await the manual instruction.

The manual instruction is still not available to me: an unnamed gesture is not actionable, and the changing light does not justify a guess. I will keep the bomb untouched. I am giving the Mute a precise two-sign code and asking the Deaf to name the signs literally, rather than reporting an uninterpreted placeholder.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send exactly two gestures for the current state. First: 👍 means CUT and 👎 means DO NOT CUT. Second, only if the first is 👍: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, and 👌 means wire 3. Deaf, report the literal gesture names you see, in order; do not interpret or omit them.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light green; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent only ? again. No wire number or cut instruction is established; do not cut.

The current state is display 0 with a green light and unchanged wire colours. The Mute’s latest gesture is still not identified, so neither the action nor a wire position is established. I will not cut based on the light sequence or infer a rule. I am narrowing the protocol to one unmistakably named gesture at a time: the Mute should send the action first, and only after a confirmed cut action send the wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For this exact state, send only one gesture: 👍 means CUT, 👎 means DO NOT CUT. Deaf, report the gesture by its literal name, not as a question mark. If and only if it is 👍, send the wire separately: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light blue; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again sent only ?. No wire number or cut instruction is established; do not cut.

The bomb remains unchanged except for the light, and I still have no reliable manual instruction or wire number. The repeated `?` conveys only that a gesture occurred, not which gesture it was, so cutting would be an unsafe guess. I will continue waiting rather than detonate the bomb.

```text
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; light orange; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute again sent only ? to me. No wire number or cut instruction is established; do not cut.

The display and wire colours remain unchanged, while the light is now orange. The Mute’s signal is still arriving to me only as an unidentified mark, so there is no safe action or wire choice. I will ask the Deaf, through a visible sign, to relay the Mute’s gesture literally rather than interpret it.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```
